title: Annealing in variational inference mitigates mode collapse: a theoretical study on Gaussian mixtures
claim: Naive training from narrow or covering initializations collapses onto one mode, while a gradual temperature schedule recovers all modes.
layout: 3x5 grid; rows are scenarios, columns are training time plus variance plot
description: A 3-row by 5-column grid of line plots. Rows are labeled Vanilla VI with standard init, Vanilla VI with covering init, and Annealed VI. The first four columns show 1D marginal densities at t=0, tf/3, 2tf/3 and tf. The target π (solid blue) is a bimodal mixture with a small left mode and a large right mode. The learned q_θ (red dashed) is overlaid. In rows 1 and 2, q_θ ends up covering only the large right mode, so the small mode is missed. In row 3, q_θ starts flat and gradually splits, finally matching both modes. The fifth column plots variance dynamics in gray against the β⁻¹ reference line: it is near 1 in row 1, decays from 10² in row 2, and falls linearly on a log scale in row 3. The eye goes to the red-versus-blue curve mismatch in the final column of the first two rows versus the last row.
caption: Preliminary experiments: annealing mitigates mode collapse. The first 4 columns show the marginal density along the direction of µ∗of both π and qθ, at 4 different training stages. The fifth column shows the variance dynamics. Each row represents a different scenario; from top to bottom: no annealing with σ1,2 initialized to one, no annealing with covering initial distribution (high initial variances σ1,2 ≫R), annealing with schedule given by eq. abstract: Mode collapse, the failure to capture one or more modes when targeting a multimodal distribution, is a central challenge in modern variational inference. In this work, we provide a mathematical analysis of annealing based strategies for mitigating mode collapse in a tractable setting: learning a Gaussian mixture, where mode collapse is known to arise. Leveraging a low dimensional summary statistics description, we precisely characterize the interplay between the initial temperature and the annealing rate, and derive a sharp formula for the probability of mode collapse. Our analysis shows that an appropriately chosen annealing scheme can robustly prevent mode collapse. Finally, we present numerical evidence that these theoretical tradeoffs qualitatively extend to neural network based models, RealNVP normalizing flows, providing guidance for designing annealing strategies mitigating mode collapse in practical variational inference pipelines.
